Lessons.Title: The Nearest Multiples of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will determine the nearest multiple of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000 and a given multi-digit whole number.
Before this lesson, you named multiples of 10,000 and 100,000 that are near given numbers and identified the closest ones. You reasoned visually—by locating the numbers on a number line and approximating your distance from adjacent tick marks that indicate ten-thousands, or from endpoints that mark hundred-thousands. In this lesson, you begin to reason numerically—by thinking about the value of the digits in a number to determine its nearest multiple of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000.
Core relationship: Nearest multiples of 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000. Compare distances to adjacent multiples on an equal-interval line.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Estimation Exploration: What Could It Be?	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Closer to This or That?	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Closer to Which Number?	 [OPTIONAL] (10 minutes); Activity 3:  What’s the Nearest Multiple?	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  The Nearest Multiples	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: How far is 374,500 above 370,000?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Is 374,500 closer to 370,000 or 380,000?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Choosing the closest multiple only by the first digit.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare distances to adjacent multiples on an equal-interval line.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Rounding 348,620 to 348,000 without checking the upper endpoint.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The stated place value, scale, or arithmetic relationship is not preserved.
CommonMistakes.Correction: 349,000 is only 380 away, whereas 348,000 is 620 away.
